MessageStrip.text: Cost Efficiency answers the business question: is the receipt airfare reasonable compared with comparable DMO flight prices, and should the company accept, review, or reject the cost?

StandardListItem.title: Global business question
StandardListItem.description: This tab answers whether the receipt airfare is economically reasonable compared with available DMO flight alternatives. It also says whether the answer is final, partial, or not assessable.

StandardListItem.title: Input used
StandardListItem.description: It uses the receipt's extracted travel ID, flight legs and airfare items, then loads the DMO travel and bookings itself. It does not simply reuse the visible result from Match Travel Data.

StandardListItem.title: Receipt integrity first
StandardListItem.description: Before judging cost efficiency, the service checks each extracted receipt flight leg against DMO bookings by carrier, connection or flight number, date, and route. Unmatched legs make the result suspicious or partial.

StandardListItem.title: Benchmark comparison
StandardListItem.description: For each credible flight leg, the selected receipt or DMO booked fare is compared with comparable DMO flight alternatives. The benchmark can be exact, expanded by date, or expanded by nearby airports depending on the filter settings.

StandardListItem.title: Decision produced
StandardListItem.description: The tab converts the comparison into GOOD, ACCEPTABLE, REVIEW, INSUFFICIENT_DATA, PARTIAL_ONLY, or NOT_ASSESSABLE. If receipt integrity is suspicious, the final economic decision is blocked and only partial benchmark values are shown.

StandardListItem.title: Currency handling
StandardListItem.description: The source currency shows the original purchase view. The company decision currency shows the normalized view used for the final business decision.

StandardListItem.title: Boundary of this tab
StandardListItem.description: This tab does its own booking selection for cost assessment. It can verify, partially assess, or reject a receipt based on whether extracted receipt legs are found in DMO bookings. It does not prove the employee/customer identity as deeply as Match Travel Data.

StandardListItem.title: Fallback case
StandardListItem.description: If the receipt has no structured flight legs, the service cannot verify individual legs. In that case it uses all DMO travel bookings and marks the result as needing careful review, not as a strongly verified decision.

StandardListItem.title: Expand benchmark (Flights)
StandardListItem.description: Minimum number of comparable flights wanted before the benchmark is considered strong. If fewer flights are found, the benchmark search can be expanded.

StandardListItem.title: ± days
StandardListItem.description: Allows comparison flights from nearby travel dates when the exact flight date does not provide enough comparables.

StandardListItem.title: Radius nearby (km)
StandardListItem.description: In the main benchmark, nearby airports can strengthen a thin comparison market while exact-route flights remain preferred. The separate opportunity explorer uses the same GPS radius but excludes the original route completely.

StandardListItem.title: Acceptable
StandardListItem.description: Tolerance used for the business decision. Example: if the selected airfare is within the accepted percentage over the benchmark, it can still be acceptable.

StandardListItem.title: Currency Decision
StandardListItem.description: Currency used for the final company view. This makes decisions comparable even when the receipt source currency is different.

MessageStrip.text: Tune the benchmark search before running Assess Cost. These values control how broad the comparison market becomes.

This block answers: can the receipt be trusted for cost assessment? Only matched and credible receipt flight legs should be used for the benchmark. Unmatched legs are listed separately so the final decision does not hide suspicious data.

Panel.headerText: How to read one flight leg

StandardListItem.title: Selected total
StandardListItem.description: The amount being assessed for this grouped leg. It can come from the matched booking or receipt airfare, depending on the backend result.

StandardListItem.title: Benchmark total
StandardListItem.description: The comparison price selected from comparable DMO flight alternatives for the same or expanded market.

StandardListItem.title: Passengers
StandardListItem.description: Number of receipt-relevant passengers included in this grouped leg. This prevents other passengers on the same travel from inflating the cost decision.

StandardListItem.title: Status
StandardListItem.description: Leg-level decision showing whether this selected leg cost is acceptable compared with the benchmark and threshold.

StandardListItem.title: Alternatives
StandardListItem.description: Benchmark, cheapest, reference, and all alternatives explain why the benchmark was chosen and what other comparable prices were available.

Button.tooltip: Run the optional nearby-airport comparison. It does not change the main Cost Efficiency decision.

MessageStrip.text: Optional advisory tool: it excludes the original booked route completely and searches for different routes through nearby airports found from GPS coordinates. Its result never changes the main Cost Efficiency decision.

Panel.headerText: What does this additional check bring?

StandardListItem.title: Separate from the official decision
StandardListItem.description: The normal benchmark answers whether the purchased fare was commercially reasonable for the booked route. This explorer only adds supporting evidence and never overwrites GOOD, ACCEPTABLE, REVIEW, or NOT_ASSESSABLE.

StandardListItem.title: Original route is excluded
StandardListItem.description: For EWR → MIA, this check deliberately removes EWR → MIA and searches routes such as JFK → MIA, EWR → FLL, or JFK → FLL.

StandardListItem.title: GPS radius becomes visible
StandardListItem.description: The service reads airport latitude and longitude from the enriched database, calculates distances, and shows which origin and destination airports were found inside the selected radius.

StandardListItem.title: Adjusted commercial comparison
StandardListItem.description: A cheaper flight is not automatically better. The tool adds an estimated extra cost for each changed airport and passenger, then calculates gross saving, adjusted cost, and net saving.

StandardListItem.title: Materiality thresholds
StandardListItem.description: Only a net saving that reaches both the configured amount and percentage is marked as a material opportunity. Smaller differences remain informational.

StandardListItem.title: Historical limitation
StandardListItem.description: The result uses the available DMO flight catalog. Without stored historical offer snapshots, it cannot prove that an alternative was actually available when the ticket was originally purchased.
